the_signal.headline: Fine-tuning vs RAG: Production LLM systems need both
the_signal.body: n8n's analysis cuts through the false choice between fine-tuning and RAG—most production revenue systems use both, not either/or. GTM engineers shipping AI agents need to stop debating and start architecting hybrid approaches that balance accuracy (fine-tuning) with freshness (RAG). This is the difference between demo performance and production reliability.

thread_of_day.title: SQLite in Production: WAL Mode, Concurrency, and VFS Layers
thread_of_day.takeaway: SQLite is becoming viable for revenue-critical systems when optimized for concurrency—relevant for GTM engineers building lightweight agents that need reliable state without PostgreSQL overhead.

quote.text: Organizations do not advance evenly through AI maturity levels. There is a specific transition point where most orgs catastrophically skip levels.
quote.source: n8n Blog: AI Maturity - Bridging the Orchestration Chasm

whats_moving.topic: Fine-tuning vs RAG for production LLMs
whats_moving.context: The binary debate is dead—n8n's analysis confirms production systems need both approaches layered together for accuracy and freshness.
SOC and security teams are moving RAG + threat intelligence into automated incident workflows, expanding AI revenue systems beyond customer-facing use cases.
Lightweight databases are re-entering revenue systems as concurrency and WAL optimizations make them viable for agent state and execution logs.

act_on_this: Audit your current agent architecture: if you're using only RAG or only fine-tuning, design a hybrid layer this sprint. Start with a single revenue-critical workflow and benchmark retrieval accuracy + latency before/after adding fine-tuned reasoning.

numbers.stat: 75 capabilities expected in production agent development tools; most platforms only deliver ~40.
numbers.context: You're shipping incomplete agent infrastructure if you haven't inventoried the 35-capability gap—this is where production execution reliability fails.
